name: evershop
compareNote: 164 tests, Postgres. Their config: 1 worker, fullyParallel false ('Shared DB'); the kind of suite isolate is for

db.migrate: cd ../.. && (PORT=39217 node packages/evershop/dist/bin/start/index.js & pid=$!; ok=1; for i in $(seq 1 180); do if curl -sf -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:39217/; then ok=0; break; fi; sleep 1; done; kill $pid; wait $pid; exit $ok)

notes: Their setup (tests/e2e/README.md): `npm run dev` in the repo root against a local Postgres, then `npm test` in tests/e2e with BASE_URL, DATABASE_URL and PLAYWRIGHT_WORKERS=1 (.env.example: 'e2e tests share the same DB, so parallelism is limited'). The recipe runs the production build (`npm run build` + start) instead of the dev server, in both arms; the baseline arm is `isolate run --baseline --app`: one app, one database, their config's worker count.
Migration: EverShop migrates on startup (the Docker install path; `evershop install` refuses to run when DB_HOST is set), so the migrate step boots the app once on port 39217 and stops it.

globalSetup creates a throw-away admin user in the database and saves its session cookie to .auth/admin.json. Under isolate it runs once against w0, and w0 is then copied to every worker (DECISIONS D-015), so the cookie is valid on every worker's app.
The app builds absolute links as http://localhost:<port>, so app.urlHost is localhost: with 127.0.0.1 the admin cookie was not sent to those links and saves failed.
The cloud file-storage specs (15 tests) skip themselves without S3/Azure/GCS credentials, in both arms.
CYPRESS_INSTALL_BINARY=0: the root devDependencies include Cypress, which the Playwright suite does not use.

Flaky in both arms (sandbox, 2026-09-28): drag-drop page-builder specs fail in some runs of either arm; page-builder specs can hit EverShop's own rate limiter (120 /api requests per minute per IP, in memory per app) and fail with 429. See data/results/evershop/compare-sandbox-2026-09-28.txt.

noRateLimit.note: EverShop's in-memory rate limiter (per IP, per app process: 120 /api requests a minute, 300 pages a minute, 8 logins or sign-ups per 15 minutes) is off in every arm. It turns itself off only under NODE_ENV=test, which also moves sessions into the app's memory, so the compiled middleware file is patched to skip it when ISOLATE_NO_RATE_LIMIT=1.
